description: Executive summary for the NFL Lines & Strategy hub. Verified anchors carry sources; gaps are listed explicitly and linked to the Flagged for Review page.
title: NFL Lines & Strategy — Executive Summary
purpose: Decision-support research system that originates NFL lines, develops and validates betting-signal strategies, ranks them on a skill-based leaderboard, and tracks injuries and starter/backup roster state. Not a wagering service.

verifiedAnchors.anchor: NFL 2026 fixtures, kickoff times, venues and records are available from the official league schedule.
Official NFL Injury Report publishes player, position, injury, practice status and game status weekly per team.
The official 2026 NFL Rulebook governs game timing, overtime and roster/designation rules.
Official player statistics and Next Gen Stats play-level data are available for model inputs and correlation.
Official division/conference/league standings are published with W-L-T and point differential.
Bet mechanics (single bet, parlay, proposition bet) are defined by official state gaming regulators.
Player-prop action requires the named player to play; parlay legs must each win for the ticket to pay.

whatWeHave: A full requirements list (R1-R29) decomposed from the brief.
A clear open-questions inventory (Q1-Q12) with explicit have / don't-have splits.
A suggestions register (SU1-SU15) to improve decision-making and discover missing information, with a review workflow.
A strategy framework covering single bet, parlay and player-prop combinations (ST1-ST6).
A defined methodology for validation gates, correlation, luck removal and ranking (M1-M7).
A leaderboard design with eligibility, ranking metric, tie-breaks and reward tiers.
An injury/roster starter-backup signal model with verified example rows from the official Week 10 injury report.
An official, verified source registry (S1-S10) and a flagged-for-review register (FL1-FL10).
A line-by-line verification script that fails the build on unsourced or unflagged-blank rows.
whatWeDontHave: A locked operating jurisdiction and a single settlement rule set (Q1, Q10).
Machine-readable official feeds for depth charts, rosters and injury history, with confirmed cadence/latency (Q2, Q8).
A trained, calibrated line-origination model and market-implied calibration (Q7).
Empirical correlation values computed from official play-level data (Q4).
Validated strategy performance; no strategy has passed the validation gates yet (Q5, FL5).
A historical injury/roster archive sufficient for back-testing (Q8).
keyDecisionsNeeded: Lock the operating jurisdiction and settlement rule set (Q1).
Select and test the official data feeds for injury, roster and depth charts (Q2).
Approve the skill metric and validation-gate thresholds (Q3, Q5).
Approve the leaderboard metric and reward structure (Q6).
Confirm v1 scope of bet types and markets (Q12).
Review and approve or reject the proposed suggestions (SU1-SU15).
methodSummary: Strategies must pass configurable validation gates (out-of-sample, no look-ahead, edge vs market, selectivity, significance). Correlation is estimated from play-level data and applied when combining legs. Luck is removed by out-of-sample testing, ranking on edge vs market / closing-line value, selectivity requirements and risk-adjusted returns. Lines are model-originated and clearly labelled.
disclaimer: This is decision-support research, not a wagering service. No real-money wagers are placed. Betting carries risk; please gamble responsibly.
